page.text:
Under the relation of logical equivalence ($\Leftrightarrow$),
propositions satisfy a rich system of algebraic identities. In fact, when
propositions are identified modulo equivalence, the resulting
mathematical structure is a *Boolean algebra*—an algebraic system sharing
deep structural parallels with the algebra of sets under intersection,
union, and complementation.

The first foundational law is the *law of double negation*: denying a
denial restores the original assertion. In classical logic, where every
statement is either true or false, there is no third epistemic status;
hence, to demonstrate that it is false that $P$ is false is to establish
that $P$ is true. This equivalence underpins the method of proof by
contradiction.
